target.title: fix(codex): heartbeat notifications to other channels are silently denied by cross-context policy
target.body:
Closes #102206

> **AI-assisted PR.** Authored with Claude (Opus 4.8). I have reviewed the change and understand what it does.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent running on the embedded Codex backend would have its autonomous notifications to other channels **silently denied**. Since v2026.6.9, heartbeat and cron polls, plus `sessions_send`-injected inter-session handoffs, cannot send a message to a different provider (e.g. a heartbeat notification to Discord) — the send is dropped by the cross-context messaging guard with no user-visible error. In the reporting environment this silently lost **71 real notifications over ~2.5 weeks**.

The affected surface is autonomous/background delivery from a Codex-backed agent (heartbeat, cron, inter-session handoff) to any channel other than the one the agent's main session is nominally on. Interactive WebChat UI conversations are not the trigger and their behavior is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Mechanism.** Since v2026.6.9 the Codex app-server dynamic-tool bridge passes `currentChannelProvider: resolveCodexMessageToolProvider(params)` into the hook context. The resolver returned `messageChannel ?? messageProvider`. For internal turns delivered into an agent's main session — heartbeat/cron polls and `sessions_send`-injected inter-session handoffs — the embedded backend passes both fields as the internal `webchat` channel (`INTERNAL_MESSAGE_CHANNEL`); see `src/tui/embedded-backend.ts:740-741`. `enforceCrossContextPolicy` then treats the run as *bound to a real `webchat` conversation* and denies an autonomous cross-provider send:

```
Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target provider "discord" while bound to "webchat".
```

v2026.6.8 passed **no** binding on the Codex path, so the guard no-op'd (`if (!currentTarget) return`). v2026.6.9 introduced the binding and thus the regression (bisected 6.8-OK → 6.9-DENIED in the same session).

**Fix.** `resolveCodexMessageToolProvider` now returns `undefined` when **both** hold: (a) the resolved provider is the internal message channel (`isInternalMessageChannel`), and (b) the turn is an internal turn — `trigger === "heartbeat" | "cron"`, or `inputProvenance.kind === "inter_session"` (new exported helper `isInternalCodexMessageTurn`). This restores the pre-v2026.6.9 "no binding" behavior for exactly the turns that regressed.

**Why the turn-kind discriminator is the narrowest correct scope.** Dropping the binding *only* for internal turns on the internal channel leaves every real conversation bound:
- Real WebChat UI conversations carry a `user`/`manual` trigger and no inter-session provenance, so they **stay bound** — cross-provider containment for the genuine user-facing surface is unchanged.
- Internal turns delivered on a real deliverable channel (e.g. `telegram`) are not on the internal `webchat` channel, so they also **stay bound**.
- Only the spurious binding to the non-deliverable internal channel — which never represented a real conversation to contain against — is removed. `toolPolicyMessageProvider` still carries the raw channel, so channel-level tool policy resolution is unaffected.

This aligns the Codex path with the non-Codex core path, which never binds internal turns to the internal channel in the first place. The same resolver feeds both `run-attempt.ts` and `side-question.ts`, so both Codex code paths are covered by the single change.

## User Impact

Operators running agents on the embedded Codex backend get their autonomous notifications delivered again: heartbeat and cron runs, and inter-session (`sessions_send`) handoffs, can once more send to channels other than the agent's nominal channel (Discord, Telegram, etc.) instead of being silently suppressed. No configuration change is required, and no new denial or prompt-injection surface is opened — interactive WebChat UI conversations keep the exact same cross-provider containment they have today.

## Relationship to #102216 / #102217

Two PRs are already open on #102206. Both are worthwhile attempts at the same regression; this one differs in what it fixes and what it preserves.

- **#102216** (@lin-hongkuan) returns `messageProvider` when `messageChannel === "webchat" && messageProvider !== "webchat"`. This does not fix the reported bug: embedded-backend internal runs pass **both** fields as `INTERNAL_MESSAGE_CHANNEL` (`src/tui/embedded-backend.ts:740-741`), so `messageProvider` is also `"webchat"` and the guard condition never triggers for a real heartbeat/cron/inter-session turn — the resolver still returns `"webchat"` and the send is still denied. Its added test uses `{ messageChannel: "webchat", messageProvider: "discord" }`, a combination internal runs do not produce.
- **#102217** (@xydigit-zt, [AI]) strips `"webchat"` from the resolver **unconditionally**. That does fix the denial, but it also removes the binding for genuine WebChat UI user conversations, loosening cross-provider containment for a real user-facing surface (the PR carries `merge-risk: 🚨 compatibility`). This PR scopes the drop to internal turns only (`isInternalCodexMessageTurn`), so real WebChat UI turns keep their binding and containment is unchanged.

In short: this change fixes the exact turns that regressed (which #102216 misses) without loosening the guard for real user conversations (which #102217 does).

## Evidence

**1. Production occurrence.** See the live logs in #102206: 71 lost notifications over ~2.5 weeks, the exact denial string above, and the bisection showing the same session going 6.8-OK → 6.9-DENIED.

**2. Real-runtime differential** (compiled `dist`, default-deny config, no `crossContext` overrides). `enforceCrossContextPolicy` is byte-identical across the two builds — only the resolver changed. A harness drove the real pipeline `resolveCodexMessageToolProvider → enforceCrossContextPolicy({ action: "send", channel: "discord", ... })`:

| Turn | BEFORE (installed OpenClaw 2026.6.11, `e085fa1`) | AFTER (this branch, `b279803`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Heartbeat → `discord` | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **throws** `Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target provider "discord" while bound to "webchat".` | resolver → `undefined`; gate no-ops; **send passes** |
| Inter-session (`sessions_send`) → `discord` | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **throws** (same denial) | resolver → `undefined`; **send passes** |
| **Control:** genuine WebChat *user* turn → `discord` | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **DENIED** | resolver → `"webchat"`; gate **DENIED** (containment for the real UI surface unchanged) |

(Real Discord channel ids redacted as `channel:<redacted>`.)

Note: full-gateway E2E was not run because the embedded Codex credential is keychain-backed OAuth and is not isolatable without touching the production keychain. The changed logic is fully exercised at the provider layer, where the regression lives.

**3. Tests.** 6 new regression tests:

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.test.ts`
- `keeps the internal channel bound for real webchat user turns`
- `drops the internal channel binding for heartbeat and cron turns`
- `drops the internal channel binding for sessions_send inter-session turns`
- `keeps a real delivery channel bound even for internal triggers`
- `classifies internal-turn kinds for cross-context binding`

`extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts`
- `does not bind the message tool to the internal channel for internal turns`

Focused vitest green: `dynamic-tool-build` 56/56, `run-attempt` 118/118, `outbound-policy` 25/25. `pnpm build` green.

---

- [x] Confirm you understand what the code does
